course_name_original: Ingeniería de Procesos de Conformado con Conservación de Materiales (21720037)
prerequisites: Having passed the courses Manufacturing Engineering and Manufacturing Technologies

learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and evaluate the performance of Material-Conserving Forming Processes. Be introduced to CAE Technologies in the field of material-conserving forming processes.

Acquisition by the student of the basic knowledge that allows them to conveniently address problems related to establishing the optimal conditions necessary to carry out a specific manufacturing process that involves material-conserving forming processes: selection and identification of technologies, equipment, and processes; design of the global process; analysis, evaluation, and improvement of process performance from economic, energy, and environmental points of view.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of metal powder forming processes
Fundamentals of Metal Casting. Gravity Casting Pouring
Analysis of Sand Molding techniques and Sand Types
Analysis of Metal Mold Molding processes
Analysis of Lost Model Molding processes
Block 4 - Thermoplastic and Thermoset Forming Processes
Analysis of plastic injection molding processes
Analysis of plastic blow molding processes
Analysis of plastic rotational molding processes
Analysis of manual and automatic thermoset forming processes

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment: Workshop Practice Attendance and Submission of Practice Reports
Continuous Assessment: Theoretical/Practical Tests and/or Assignments
Continuous Assessment: Attendance at Theory, Theoretical-Practical Classes, and Tutorials. Completion of theoretical topic attention tests.

assessment_rules: Students are continuously assessed through three components: workshop practice attendance and submission of practice reports (20% of total grade), theoretical/practical tests and/or assignments (50% of total grade), and attendance at theory, theoretical-practical classes, tutorials, and theoretical topic attention tests (30% of total grade). The course does not explicitly state minimum marks for components or resit arrangements.
